item.title: Cyber Analyst in CYBER DEFENCE CENTRE
item.description: Cyber Analyst, Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. Whilst the team is primarily located in the Bank's London office in Threadneedle Street, the team does also have a presence in the Leeds office. This posting is therefore open to London OR Leeds applicants. Department overview: Within the Cyber Security Division you will be working with people who are passionate about protecting the security and stability of our Technology estate. Whether it is identifying threats, uncovering vulnerabilities or ensuring robust and resilient infrastructure, you’ll be working at the cutting edge in a security-centric organisation. You’ll focus on ensuring security by design, and ensuring we have safe, stable and resilient systems. Collaborating closely with colleagues across Technology and throughout the organisation you will help the division safeguard critical systems and information. Our award-winning specialist teams are committed to developing their expertise in a constantly evolving environment. Aligned to industry best-practice, staff are encouraged to develop their skills both internally and externally, through mentoring, training and formal qualifications. Job description The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. The CDC is made up of four key domains: Capability, Threat, Detection Engineering and Defence Operations. Reporting to the Cyber Defence Operations Lead Operations lead in the Cyber Defence Operations (CDO) function, The successful candidate will take part in the operations rota ensuring security alerts are thoroughly investigated, escalated appropriately and take part in subsequent Cyber Security incident response activities as part of the wider Cyber Security incident response team where required. When not responding to security alerts or incidents, as part of the CDO function, the role holder will be expected to proactively seek opportunities to improve the team’s operational capability for both detection and response processes through a greater use of automation. The role will require close collaboration across all of the CDC’s core functions and has varied and challenging day-to-day responsibilities, as well as exposure to a range of cutting-edge technology in cyber security, data analytics and cyber threat intelligence. Key Experience / Skills Minimum: Good understanding of best practice security incident response concepts and approaches Practical experience in technical cyber security incident response methodologies Excellent written and verbal communication skills Essential: Experience working in Security Operations Centre with specific experience triaging security alerts and an understanding of wider cyber security incident response practices. Knowledge of computer network fundamentals, including network protocols and infrastructure (packet capture analysis, firewalls, web proxies, DNS etc.) Ability to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner Ability and willingness to learn new technical cyber security skills Logical mind-set Desirable: Experience developing and documenting incident response processes and designing IR playbooks. GCIH or similar qualification in Security Incident response The ability to acquire DV clearance (To be eligible to apply you must be a British citizen (either born here or naturalised) and one of your parents must be a British citizen or have substantial ties to the UK. Understanding of common cyber threats and attacker tactics, techniques and procedures and an ability to identify appropriate mitigation strategies Experience using automation or SOAR platforms Knowledge of incident response principles Experience using MITRE ATT&CK Experience using Splunk Experience using an intelligence platform Software development, scripting or programming skills Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Leeds: £40,320 - £45,360 London: £44,800 - £50,400 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. This role closes on 13 September 2026 Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in TECHNOLOGY
item.description: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London Part of the Bank’s Technology Leadership Team and reporting to the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Central Services COO, this role provides the business management, governance and operational oversight needed to run safe, secure and resilient technology services for the Bank of England. As a member of the Technology Leadership Team, you will be individually and collectively responsible for the Bank’s information technology and computer systems, through which the Bank delivers its mission. You will lead the core OCIO disciplines that enable effective technology leadership, including financial management and reporting, strategic supplier management, resource and demand management, regulatory compliance, audit coordination, risk management and performance reporting. Core to your role will be building strong relationships with the CIO, the TLT and key partners across the Bank who work closely with the Technology Directorate, including Finance, Change and Planning, People, Risk, Procurement and other central functions. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. Primary accountabilities Management of finances, performance and financial reporting • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of the financial performance of the Technology Directorate. • You work with the finance business partner and CIO to support financial and business planning, including the setting of budgets. • You define and monitor key financial, operational and supplier performance metrics, using data and insight to support prioritisation, investment decisions and transparent reporting to senior governance forums. • You are responsible for the provision of accurate and timely financial information to the CIO and to Court. Strategic supplier management • You maintain oversight of the Technology Directorate’s strategic supplier management approach, ensuring key supplier relationships are aligned to technology priorities, service resilience, commercial value and the Bank’s risk appetite. • You oversee the use of supplier segmentation, account management plans, performance scorecards and relationship reviews to ensure strategic suppliers are managed according to their criticality, value and risk profile. • You monitor strategic supplier performance, contractual obligations, service levels, key risks, improvement actions and value delivery, ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You support executive engagement with strategic suppliers, helping the Technology Leadership Team move supplier relationships beyond tactical renewals towards long-term partnership, innovation, resilience and continuous improvement. • You ensure supplier insight, market intelligence and third-party risk information are used to inform technology planning, investment decisions, commercial pipelines and future sourcing strategies Internal process management • You maintain oversight of internal business processes that support Technology Directorate productivity, service quality, cost control and timely delivery. • You evaluate existing business processes, determining and outlining business process improvements. • You work with the Technology Leadership Team and other technology leaders to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, simplification and continuous improvement across Technology Directorate operations. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to oversee the implementation of Bank-wide business process improvement initiatives. Resource and demand management • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of overall headcount within the Technology Directorate to ensure the directorate operates within its headcount budget. • You support the capacity planning process as part of the budgeting and forecasting cycle, ensuring workforce plans are aligned to technology priorities, delivery commitments and affordability. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to ensure that change programmes are resourced appropriately. Regulatory compliance • You are responsible for ensuring the Technology Directorate complies with external regulatory requirements and internal policies, including public procurement policy, technology resilience obligations and compliance relating to Critical National Infrastructure. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to regulatory requests. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a culture of compliance. Risk and audit management • You establish, maintain and review the Technology Directorate’s risk management framework, mechanisms and tools, ensuring they support consistent identification, assessment, monitoring, control and reporting of technology risk. • You support and monitor the first line of defence in applying technology risk management tools, including identifying, assessing, monitoring and controlling technology risk, and advising on proportionate mitigation measures. • You assess the adequacy and effectiveness of controls from a technology risk perspective during due diligence of new products and applications, incident handling and material change activity, providing advice and recommendations where required. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a shared understanding of risk. • You work with the TLT to support the management of Technology risks and controls. • You support the management of technology audit activity by coordinating evidence, tracking actions, monitoring closure of agreed mitigations and ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to audit requests, ensuring responses are complete, timely and aligned with agreed ownership of audit actions. Team management and management of PS/PA office • You are accountable for building knowledge, skills and best practice within your teams and across the Technology Directorate. • You are responsible for developing and mentoring a high-performing team of direct reports. Role requirements Minimum/Essential criteria • Proven experience and track record of building relationships across business units and with a range of stakeholders, balancing competing interests and generating a collaborative, one-team mindset. • Successful leadership experience, established over several years, within a high-performing central operations or COO team, or in a comparable technology business management function. • Established understanding of finance, budgeting and forecasting, with an accounting qualification desirable, and experience using financial insight to support technology investment, supplier and workforce decisions. • Established understanding of regulatory compliance, audit management and risk management in a complex technology or regulated environment. • Established understanding of internal process management and capacity and demand planning. Strong stakeholder management and interpersonal skills • You have very strong interpersonal skills at senior levels and a proven ability to influence decisions across organisational boundaries. • You are an effective communicator, able to create a compelling narrative and inspire people to follow you. • You can build trusted relationships at all levels of the Bank, enabling you to have difficult conversations in pursuit of a common objective. You can make and recommend difficult decisions. • You are recognised as an empathetic people leader and a role model for the Bank’s leadership values, promoting an inclusive culture and working environment. An experienced ‘operator’ within a central operations team • You are an experienced technology business management operator, using financial, workforce, supplier and performance insight to influence the directorate’s budgeting and forecasting process and support delivery within agreed budgets. • You are an experienced capacity and demand planner, able to make and support recommendations about the directorate’s workforce while balancing stakeholder needs and understanding due process. • You have demonstrable understanding of regulatory compliance within a comparable organisation. • You have demonstrable understanding of risk management processes within a comparable organisation. An ambassador for the Bank • You are able to build and tap into a wide external network to learn, attract talent, and help drive the reputation of the Bank. You might represent the Bank at relevant external engagements. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. item.title: Commercial Policy Manager (Sourcing)
item.description: Location: Leeds We have an exciting new role in the Commercial Policy and Operations team at the Bank, leading how we deliver commercial sourcing policy and providing expert support and guidance to the rest of the organisation. This role is part of the Commercial division’s Policy and Operations team, who deliver the policies, processes, systems and tools needed for the Bank to undertake commercial activity. The Team The team operates partly in a matrix management style, with most people dividing their time between their area of accountability (sourcing policy in this case) and pooled resource to work on cross-team projects. This enables the team to be dynamic and responsive around workload, drive collaboration and develop leadership skills at all levels. This role will be responsible for ensuring we have effective commercial sourcing policies, processes and guidance in place, as well as leading on cross-team projects in a matrix management setup. Role Responsibilities This role will be responsible for: Setting out the forward-looking strategy for sourcing policy in the Bank, defining what is needed in this area and developing a plan to deliver it. This should include the required stakeholder management, communications, etc. Creating and maintaining the Bank’s sourcing policies and processes. These should seamlessly integrate with any other areas of the commercial lifecycle, notably supplier management, third-party risk management and responsible procurement, and integrate considerations from key stakeholders such as Legal. The policies should align with public-sector legislation (including the National Procurement Policy Statement and applicable Procurement Policy Notes) and should be regularly reviewed and updated in line with benchmarking exercises, to ensure they reflect the latest best practice, and the processes should be continually improved to maximise efficiency and effectiveness. Ensuring colleagues involved in sourcing (both inside and outside of the Commercial division) understand their role and how the policies and processes should be applied, and are enabled to do this, by producing and sourcing appropriate and tailored templates, guidance and training, and ensuring they are communicated and delivered to them. Providing sourcing policy expert advice and support for more complex and specific queries not covered by the training and guidance, in line with the latest best practice. This will also include ensuring the sourcing policies are considered as part of commercial governance and offering technical advice on these considerations. Being able to evidence progress in the Bank’s approach to sourcing through the monitoring of key sourcing KPIs, such as compliance with notice publication requirements. Writing short business cases to support having access to the Policy team’s resource pool. You will also be part of a pool of resources across the team, enabling you to lead on some of the larger cross-team projects, depending on how workload varies across areas. These projects may cover matters across the whole of the Policy and Operations’ team scope. Although this is not a people management role, you will matrix manage other colleagues in the context of the projects you will lead. In those instances, you will be responsible for defining roles and responsibilities within your projects. You will develop the team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. You will also be expected to provide feedback to their line manager about their performance during your projects. Role Requirements Minimum criteria In-depth knowledge and experience of public-sector sourcing and current legislation Demonstrable experience of writing and rolling out public-sector sourcing policies Demonstrable knowledge of the rest of the commercial lifecycle (supplier management, responsible procurement and third-party risk management) Demonstrable knowledge of where and how to source the latest best-practice trends in public-sector sourcing Experience of creating and implementing strategies and delivery plans for their area of responsibility Ability to explain and present commercial matters to non-commercial colleagues, in the context of sourcing matters Essential criteria Excellent stakeholder management skills Excellent problem-solving skills Creative and critical thinking skills Self-motivation, with past evidence of driving own workload Excellent written and verbal communication skills Customer-focused, with experience delivering high-quality service and continuous improvement. Other criteria If you do not already have it, you would be expected to achieve Level 4 CIPS (funded by the Bank). Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information Location: Leeds This role offers an annual salary range in circa. of £46,320- £52,110 (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . item.title: Senior Manager, Information Operations
item.description: The Bank of England (“the Bank”) is the UK's central bank. Our mission is to deliver monetary and financial stability for the British people. The Bank of England is a diverse organisation. Each of our 5000 people are committed to public service and dedicated to promoting the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability. Central Operations delivers critical functions that support the Bank’s effectiveness and resilience across security, procurement, sustainability and optimisation services. The Information Management division is a newly established function within Central Operations, providing integrated policy and governance, operational services and information platform leadership so information is secure, compliant, accessible and reusable. ROLE SUMMARY This role leads the Information Operations team within Information Management and serves as the Bank’s senior lead for operational information management services under the Head of Information Management. It is responsible for information access and disclosure services, records management operations, retention, review and deletion services, and the operational controls, processes and management information that support effective lifecycle delivery. The role leads the delivery and continuous improvement of core operational information management services, including Freedom of Information and Subject Access Request handling, records management operations, Red List administration, retention, review and deletion activity, and oversight of Tier 0 (self service) information controls. It provides leadership through team leaders across a multi-disciplinary operational team, ensuring services operate effectively, consistently and in line with statutory, regulatory and policy requirements, with clear operational controls, management information, escalation routes and management oversight. The role works closely with Information Policy, Information Platforms, Technology and business stakeholders to translate policy into operational processes, strengthen control effectiveness and support resilient, auditable service delivery across the information lifecycle. Key Responsibilities Operational Service Delivery and Control Lead the Bank’s operational information management services, ensuring delivery is effective, consistent and aligned with policy requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, service expectations and operational priorities. Oversee information access and disclosure services, including Freedom of Information, Subject Access Request and related operational processes, ensuring timely, accurate and well-governed delivery. Lead records management operations, including retention, review and deletion activity, ensuring processes are auditable, proportionate and consistently applied. Service Management, Risk and Continuous Improvement Establish and maintain effective service management arrangements, including prioritisation, service standards, controls, escalation routes, issue resolution and performance monitoring. Manage operational risks, issues and exceptions, ensuring material concerns are identified, escalated and addressed appropriately and that service delivery remains resilient and well controlled. Use operational data, management information and insight to improve performance, inform assurance activity and support continuous improvement across the wider Information Management function. Operational Delivery Model and Enterprise Alignment Work closely with Information Policy, Information Platforms, Technology, Legal, Privacy, Records Management and business stakeholders to embed policy and control requirements in operational processes and enterprise information platforms. Improve operational processes, workflows and service design to reduce manual effort, increase consistency and strengthen end-to-end lifecycle management across information services. Support the development of sustainable operating models for information services, ensuring roles, responsibilities and hand-offs are clear and effective across teams. Leadership and People Management Lead the Information Operations function through team leaders, setting direction and priorities across a multi-disciplinary operational team, ensuring effective management oversight, clear accountability and consistent delivery across services. Develop team leaders and build a strong culture of service, control, accountability and continuous improvement across the wider team. Minimum Criteria Experience leading operational information management, records management, disclosure, or relevant comparable services in a complex or regulated organisation. Experience establishing or running operational services with defined processes, controls, service standards, prioritisation and performance oversight. Experience managing statutory, regulatory or policy-led operational requirements, for example in records management, data protection, Freedom of Information, Subject Access Requests or similar controlled services. Experience leading teams through managers or team leaders, with accountability for delivery, control and service improvement. Essential Criteria Strong judgement and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage operational risk, resolve issues and escalate appropriately in a controlled environment. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain complex issues, trade-offs and priorities clearly to different audiences. Ability to lead through others, build capability in managers or team leaders and foster a culture of accountability, service and continuous improvement. Ability to work across organisational boundaries and translate policy, control or legal requirements into practical and proportionate operational delivery. Desirable Criteria Knowledge of records management, data protection, Freedom of Information and Subject Access Request requirements within a broader information management framework. Familiarity with enterprise information environments such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Purview or related technologies from an operational, records or disclosure perspective. Experience improving or redesigning operational processes to strengthen control, consistency or service efficiency. Experience working in a large, complex institutional environment and navigating multiple stakeholder groups, governance requirements and operational dependencies. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. ___ Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. For most roles where work can be carried out at home, we aim for colleagues to spend half of their time in the office, with a minimum of 40% per month. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65 or 1/50) or decrease (to 1/95 or 1/105) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. item.title: Senior Associate – Freedom of Information Appeals
item.description: Senior Associate – Freedom of Information Appeals Division – Communications Department – Internal Communications, External Affairs & Public Information Team – Information Disclosure Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £43,300 to £60,000 and London from £46,400 to £64,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Corporate Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. In the Communications division at the FCA we change opinions and behaviours to enable a fair and thriving financial services market for the good of consumers and the economy. It’s an exciting time as we’re expanding our team and changing how we do things to deliver more engaging, insight-led, audience focused communications. If you want to be part of a supportive and fun team, work across a wide range of issues and are ready to be challenged, curious and creative then come and join us. The Information Disclosure and Appeals teams are responsible for managing Freedom of Information (FOI) requests, personal data access requests and related appeals. The team plays a key role in helping the FCA meet its statutory obligations, supporting our transparency agenda and ensuring compliance with information rights legislation. This role is critical in managing legal, regulatory and reputational risk, as failure to meet statutory deadlines could result in action from the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and impact confidence in the FCA as a regulator. Role responsibilities Manage FOIA appeals, including Internal Reviews, Information Commissioner investigations and First-tier Tribunal (Information Rights) appeals. Support the wider Information Disclosure team with the Publication Scheme, data protection witness statements and Re-use of Public Sector Information requests Produce high quality oral and written communications to key stakeholders and to members of the public (Requesters) Provide expert advice, training and guidance to stakeholders across the FCA, promoting awareness of FOIA requirements and ensuring the organisation remains informed of legislative and regulatory developments Oversee the triage and allocation of work, ensuring service levels and agreed SLAs are met Line manage and develop junior colleagues through coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing, while acting as a key escalation point for complex and high-profile cases Skills required Minimum: Exceptional writing and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to explain complex disclosure-related issues to diverse audiences FOIA legislation experience and good knowledge of the ICO code of practice Experience researching regulatory developments and analysing information from multiple sources to identify risks, trends and emerging issues Essential: Excellent organisational skills with the ability to meet deadlines while maintaining high service standards Meticulous attention to detail in drafting responses, coupled with sound decision-making abilities Proven ability to build strong relationships and networks across an organisation to ensure a cohesive approach and timely delivery Ability to influence senior stakeholders through clear and persuasive guidance Proficiency in document redaction using various applications and software Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, coach, develop and motivate teams effectively Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. item.description: Digital Project Manager Full time / Part time Salary: £ 44,297 - £ 49,813 pa, with potential for further progression to £ 56,082 pa with our pay progression scheme. Location: Manchester Contracted to our Wilmslow office , we will be relocating to Manchester city centre from 28 September 2026. Once the move takes place your contracted office will be Circle Square, Manchester. Through hybrid working we offer flexible home and office-based working opportunities and there will be times when you will be expected to attend the office to collaborate with colleagues or travel due to business need. Job summary The Digital Project Manager is responsible for leading the delivery of digital, data and technology related projects across the ICO. Reporting to the Digital Programme Manager, the Digital Project Manager ensures that projects are delivered effectively, consistently, and with measurable impact. The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) is the independent regulator of information rights. In a data-driven world, we provide advice, guidance, and support to organisations enabling compliance with their obligations, as well as protecting individuals and their personal data. As an employer, we are passionate about making a positive difference to the lives and careers of our people, and we empower you to be curious, impactful, collaborative and respectful. Job description This role requires proactivity and versatility to manage delivery across the organisation, support the embedding of change and contribute to the continuous improvement of delivery practice. The Digital Project Manager will work with and empower project teams, scrum teams, manage interdependencies and risks, and ensure that delivery is aligned with organisational priorities and to governance standards. Key responsibilities: Lead the delivery of DDaT projects in alignment with organisational priorities whilst ensuring projects teams are empowered to deliver effectively. Use skills and experience to lead and direct end-to-end project delivery, working closely with roles within the digital delivery team such as Scrum Masters, User Centre Design specialists, Technical Business Analysts , Test Engineers , Product Owners and Architecture. Develop and maintain a comprehensive approach to project delivery by use of the Agile methods in a JIRA environment. Identify and proactively manage cross-organisational resource required to successfully delivery projects. Lead on the engagement with and coordination of actions across stakeholder groups within wider business. Ensure effective assurance reporting and visibility of deliverables, risks, and issues by monitoring and controlling project progress using appropriate tools, and by preparing and delivering reports and papers for project and programme boards. Where appropriate, provide leadership, coaching, challenge and guidance to ensure objectives are met and delivery is consistent across the organisation. Ensure outputs are effectively implemented and embedded within the business. Provide business process change support, coordinate communications and training activities, and work in partnership with stakeholders and benefit owners to maximise adoption and realise benefits. Facilitate lessons learned exercises, embedding findings into delivery practice to support a continuous learning culture and improve project management standards. Organise and support project events, including workshops, stakeholder briefings, and assurance activities. Person specification Essential criteria assessed at application stage: Experience of managing and delivering projects in public or private sector environments. Evidence of successful implementation of projects that deliver strategic value across varied domains including but not limited to digital, data, regulatory, and transformational workstreams Very strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to negotiate and to build and maintain good working relationships both internally and externally, up to and including senior management level. Excellent understanding and application of Agile delivery methodologies including Scrum . Good working knowledge of JIRA . Ability to deliver projects under strategic oversight, working in partnership with the Digital Programme Manager to ensure alignment with organisational priorities. Demonstrated leadership in managing project teams, with experience in coaching, mentoring, and developing capability across a matrix environment. Understanding of portfolio, programme and project governance and assurance, with the ability to contribute to reporting and decision-making processes. Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to represent project interests across governance forums and enable effective decision-making . Excellent judgement and the ability to deal with a changing environment both on a day-to-day and long-term basis. Commitment to continuous improvement, with experience in leading lessons learned exercises and embedding findings into delivery practice. Essential criteria assessed during interview: Experience of managing and delivering projects in public or private sector environments. Evidence of successful implementation of projects that deliver strategic value across varied domains including but not limited to digital, data, regulatory, and transformational workstreams Very strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to negotiate and to build and maintain good working relationships both internally and externally, up to and including senior management level. Good working knowledge of JIRA and the application of Agile Scrum. Ability to deliver projects under strategic oversight, working in partnership with the Digital Programme Manager to ensure alignment with organisational priorities. Understanding of portfolio, programme and project governance and assurance, with the ability to contribute to reporting and decision-making processes. Excellent judgement and the ability to deal with a changing environment both on a day-to-day and long-term basis. Commitment to continuous improvement, with experience in leading lessons learned exercises and embedding findings into delivery practice. Equality, diversity, and inclusion The ICO is committed to promoting and enhancing equality, diversity, and inclusion. We are focused on developing a workforce that is representative of the communities we serve and together we are building an inclusive workplace where all of our colleagues have the opportunity to make a real difference. We are championing this through our Equality Diversity and Inclusion Board together with a number of staff networks. Read more about our commitment on our website. Candidates with a disability who meet the minimum criteria for this vacancy will be invited to interview as part of the ICO’s commitment to the Disability Confident Scheme. As part of the ICO’s commitment to our EDI objectives and creating a workplace that represents the communities and societies we serve, we guarantee an interview to candidates who declare they identify as belonging from an ethnic minority background and who meet the minimum criteria for this vacancy If you are disabled or have an impairment and require an alternative application method, please email the HR team at recruitment@ico.org.uk Closing Date Please submit your CV and cover letter by 23:59, Thursday 17 September Your cover letter should be no more than 1,000 words and should clearly demonstrate how you meet the essential criteria for the role. Job summary As part of the Digital, Data and Technology Services (DDaT) team, you will be responsible for driving the testing activities within in a given project/product; ensuring that new and amended systems, configurations, packages, or services, together with any interfaces, perform as specified (including security requirements) and ensure that the risks associated with deployment are adequately understood and documented. In a data-driven world, we provide advice, guidance, and support to organisations enabling compliance with their obligations, as well as protecting individuals and their personal data. Job description You will review requirements and specifications and define test conditions. Interpret, execute and record test cases in accordance with test plans. Identify and report issues and risks within related product. To develop an understanding of the role of testing within product/service development, as a tool for design improvement as well as a validation process. Key responsi bilities : Reviewing requirements and specifications and defining test conditions Designing and executing test plans and carry out exploratory testing as part of a broader risk-based approach. Designing, writing and maintaining automated test scripts and suites. Designing and writing automated test strategy. Providing reports on progress, anomalies, risks and issues associated with the overall project. Knowledge of the WCAG 2.2 standards and how to test against them to spot problems and opportunities that ensure all our digital services work for all users Person specification Essential criteria assessed at application stage: ITIL qualification Knowledge of Jira/Confluence, Agile Scrum Experience designing, developing and maintaining automated test scripts working with an automated test tool. Proven experience of working with Agile and Waterfall methodologies Proven experience of working within an Agile framework. item.title: Future Payment Systems & Infrastructure Senior Associate
item.description: Job title: Future Payment Systems & Infrastructure Senior Associate Department: Payment Systems Market Interventions Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,200 and London from £59,200 to £73,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Katie via Katherine.Baker@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the PSR and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Follow this link to find out more About The PSR. Operationally the PSR is currently an independent subsidiary of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), however in March 2025 the Prime Minister announced that the PSR would be consolidated into the FCA, a pragmatic next step in simplifying regulation of payments. This transition will likely take some time and will follow a Government consultation, although the Government has already been clear that payment systems must continue to be effectively regulated. For the time being, therefore, the PSR continues to focus on delivering its important and impactful programme of work, collaborating closely with the FCA. The Future Payment Systems and Infrastructure team you are applying to join will ultimately move into the FCA when the new legislation takes effect. Candidates should be aware, therefore, that there may be changes to their responsibilities as consolidation into the FCA progresses. This is an exciting opportunity to join the PSR's Future Payment Systems and Infrastructure team, helping to shape the future of the UK's retail payments landscape. The role will support the PSR's contribution to the National Payments Vision, engagement with new and emerging payment systems, and the development of a consistent, transparent regulatory approach as oversight transitions into the FCA. Working closely with other authorities, industry participants and senior stakeholders, you will play a key role in regulatory cooperation, policy delivery and influencing the future oversight of payment systems to support better outcomes for consumers, businesses and the wider economy. Role responsibilities Working in collaboration with other authorities and payment systems participants on key issues for the National Payments Vision Contributing to the PSR’s approach to new and developing payment systems Building a deep understanding of payment systems including emerging models, their operating environments, business strategies and governance arrangements Using this understanding to contribute to robust regulatory assessment and the delivery of improved outcomes for users of payment systems Building effective working relationships with key internal stakeholders and teams whose work is material to delivery of the team’s work Promoting a culture of collaboration, inclusion and learning within the Supervision team, acting as a role model for PSR values and behaviours Skills required Minimum: Experience in a regulatory, supervisory, monitoring, compliance, policy or similar environment, with evidence of managing stakeholder relationships and contributing to regulatory, policy or compliance-related outcomes Experience analysing complex information and making recommendations, demonstrated through written reports, briefings, policy papers, assessments or similar outputs that informed decisions or actions Understanding of payment systems and/or the broader payments landscape, including how payment systems operate and support effective regulation Essential: Experience leading or taking ownership of complex projects, workstreams or policy initiatives, demonstrating accountability for delivery and outcomes Demonstrated skill in working with internal and external stakeholders, building effective partnerships and negotiating toward strategic goals Demonstrated ability to resolve complex strategic or operational problems, including identifying root causes, evaluating options and delivering proportionate, evidence-based solutions Knowledge of the economic regulation, competition and/or payments landscape, including an understanding of how regulatory frameworks impact firms, consumers and market outcomes Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical, regulatory or policy issues clearly to diverse audiences and senior stakeholders Sound judgement and decision-making capability, demonstrated through balancing risks, evidence and stakeholder considerations in challenging or ambiguous situations Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results, including planning, organising and reprioritising work to meet deadlines and quality standards Effective project management skills, including coordinating activities, managing delivery against plans and ensuring objectives are delivered within agreed timescales Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page. Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert closes: Midnight, 13 September 2026 CV Review/Shortlist: 15 September 2026 Interview: w/c 21 September 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time.

item.title: Lead Associate Lawyer
item.description: Lead Associate Lawyer Division: Legal Division Department: Law, Policy and International, Enforcement Legal Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £69,700 to £86,900 and London from £76,600 to £95,500 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate - Practising legal Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Our Legal Division provides advice and legal services across the full breadth of FCA activity, including regulatory, policy, enforcement and operational work. This Lead Associate position is in the Law and International team, which is part of the Law, Policy and International Department within Enforcement Legal. The department provides strategic, legal and policy advice on enforcement powers and policies and international enforcement engagement. The Law and International team owns the FCA’s strategy on international enforcement matters and is responsible for managing and developing key international enforcement relationships. We advise on, among other matters, the use of FCA investigation powers on behalf of overseas authorities, the disclosure of confidential information and the disclosure of personal data in an international enforcement context. The team also provides policy input on cooperation aspects of domestic legislation and legal advice on MoU work. Our associates are expected to engage with wider, cross-departmental enforcement policy work where needed. Role responsibilities Work with FCA investigation teams to advise on seeking assistance abroad and the use of evidence obtained abroad in civil, criminal and regulatory investigations and proceedings Perform initial reviews of requests for assistance received from overseas regulators. Your role is to identify all key legal issues, determine which FCA stakeholders should be made aware of the request and determine who at the FCA should respond to the request Build experience of managing more junior associates and their work. You will be expected to ensure that this work is managed and progressed effectively and to sign off key decisions for the exercise of legal powers Provide meaningful contributions to the department’s know how and guidance documents and training across the FCA, working together with the manager to ensure that legal risks are appropriately managed and work to become a specialist in agreed areas Have overall responsibility for the relationship management of several key international partners and internal stakeholders, building, maintaining and owning the relationships. This will involve regular discussions and development of a strategy to promote effective engagement, for example arranging visits and engaging others across the FCA Act as representative of Enforcement/Legal Division to senior managers and at international level, where appropriate, to ensure that the FCA’s interests are effectively represented Be accountable for advancing multiple key projects identified in collaboration with the team manager and department head. These are likely to involve complex legal issues and span the breadth of Law and International’s remit Where business need arises, associates in Law and International will work on projects relating to the wider remit of the Law, Policy and International Department Skills required Minimum: Qualified lawyer, Solicitor or Barrister of England and Wales or international equivalent Significant post-qualification experience in any of the following areas: contentious financial services or other regulatory investigations or proceedings; financial services or public law advisory work; international cooperation; complex international investigations Essential: Ability to apply sound principled legal and evidential analysis to novel situations and think strategically Well-developed relationship management skills to build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues, international counterparts and external bodies Robust, self-motivated and a good team player Ability to perform effectively in demanding situations and meet deadlines Effective communication skills to present the outcome of analysis clearly and effectively, orally and in writing Real interest in international work, cross-border cooperation and enforcement policy Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where employees work a minimum of 40% in the office each month (expectation of 50% for senior leaders). Changing from September to a minimum of 50% in the office each month (expectation of 60% for Directors and Executive Directors) A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: Agentic Payments Technical Specialist
item.description: Agentic Payments Technical Specialist Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Payments and Digital Assets Policy Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £74,900 to £88,966 and London £82,300 to £97,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Technical Specialist – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via Steve.Christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Jennifer Wishart via Jennifer.Wishart@fca.org.uk . About the FCA and Team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Payments Policy Team is a large and growing team that works closely with HMT Treasury, and colleagues across FCA and PSR, to modernise the payments regulatory framework. This includes work to realise the benefits of agentic payments, whilst maintaining a safe and trusted payments system. The payments policy team sits in Payments & Digital Assets Policy, alongside teams working on tokenised payments and crypto policy. Role Responsibilities Collaborate with teams across the FCA to lead policy work on agentic payments, shaping proposals that will directly support innovation, and impact consumers and industry Apply your deep technical expertise in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and its application to payments to the development of FCA policy and strategy both for domestic as well as international use cases for agentic payments Lead engagement with key stakeholders by building strong relationships with government, other domestic and international regulators, consumer groups, and technical experts in industry and beyond, to help shape the future of payments regulation Provide expert insight by delivering impactful advice and briefings on issues relating to agentic payments to colleagues and senior management Grow your expertise further, by developing deep knowledge of payments services and regulations and leading FCA thinking on the risks and opportunities of agentic AI and agentic payments Coach, mentor, and develop talent across the FCA, building analytical and risk management capabilities that elevate organisational performance Role model FCA values as part of the senior leadership team, fostering a culture of integrity, collaboration, and excellence Skills Required Minimum Significant professional experience in the application of agentic AI in payments Proven experience presenting complex issues clearly and succinctly to senior leaders and stakeholders, both orally and in writing Demonstratable experience of building and managing constructive relationships with key internal and external stakeholders Essential Evidence of leading complex projects, requiring strong problem solving and organisational skills, and the ability to manage a variety of competing priorities and issues An inclusive team player with experience of teaching, coaching and/or mentoring colleagues Demonstratable experience of engaging internationally on issues relating to regulation and innovation Benefits 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . item.title: PA in Insurance ED and Directors Office - Insurance Supervision
item.description: LEEDS BASED Insurance Supervision The PRA's Insurance Supervision Directorate is the largest Directorate in the PRA. We supervise over 500 UK insurance firms and branches of international insurers across life insurance, general insurance and specialist supervision. Insurance plays a vital role in supporting households, businesses and the wider economy, providing financial security and resilience when it is needed most. The sector is grappling with some of the biggest challenges facing society, from climate change and cyber risk to changing demographics, long term investment for growth, and technological innovation. As insurers adapt their business models to meet these challenges, our work continues to evolve too, making Insurance Supervision a fascinating place to work at the intersection of risk, policy, supervision and strategy. We are committed to being a high-performing, inclusive and supportive Directorate where colleagues can build fulfilling careers, develop deep expertise and make a meaningful impact on the safety and soundness of the UK financial system. Role Responsibilities A core part of the role will be the provision of high-quality administrative and business support to the Director of Insurance Supervision, to the Senior Technical Advisor and to the Private Secretary while also being part of the wider office team in supporting the wider ED & Director Office team assisting with in delivering events and key Directorate activities. We're looking for someone who is organised, approachable and proactive, with excellent communication and administrative skills. You'll enjoy managing competing priorities, working at pace and providing a high-quality service, while building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders. The role offers a unique perspective on the breadth of work taking place across Insurance Supervision. You'll work closely with senior leaders and colleagues across the Bank, while also engaging with external stakeholders including regulated firms, industry bodies, other regulators and partner organisations. You will be part of a strong and supportive PA community, with opportunities to learn, grow and build relationships across the Directorate. The breadth of the role, combined with the exposure you'll gain to senior leaders and external stakeholders, makes it an excellent platform for future career development. Role Requirements Minimum criteria Experience using the common Microsoft suite of IT programmes such as Outlook, Excel, Word, Loop, CoPilot etc Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Strong organisational, administrative and time management skills and attention to detail. Proven ability to prioritise effectively and deliver under pressure. Essential criteria Knowledge of the PRA, Bank of England or wider financial services sector. Excellent judgement and decision-making capability. Strong strategic awareness and the ability to connect the dots across complex issues. Strong influencing and relationship-building skills, including with senior stakeholders. Experience of developing and supporting people. Evidence that you can quickly pick up new and complex technical issues. Absolute discretion, integrity and professionalism. Ability to work constructively within a team. Desirable criteria Knowledge of Insurance or Supervision of the Bank of England Experience working in or covering in an ED Office / Private Office An established network across the Insurance Directorate. Understanding of governance, business planning and strategic delivery. A desire to improve processes by using technology to enhance efficiency and ways of working. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary is circa £25,760-£28,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (1) The application questions and (2) a single interview. This role closes on 29 September 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.description: LEEDS BASED 9-12 FIXED TERM CONTRACT This is a maternity contact and we would need candidates to be available to start from mid December/early January. Please do not be put off if you do not have experience in data or AI. If you meet the minimum criteria of the role, we'd still encourage an application ----------------------- About the team: ARTIS is a PRA Directorate and is formed of: the Authorisations Division, which deals with regulatory transactions where firms apply to carry out PRA regulated activities, or make changes to the activities they undertake; the Regulatory Technology, Data and Innovation Division (RDI); and the four divisions responsible for the supervision, as a host regulator, of the UK activities of banks, custodians and designated investment firms headquartered in over 50 overseas jurisdictions – including some of the world’s highest profile firms RDI’s mission is through innovation, drive forward the modernisation of technology and data usage to deliver enhancements in the efficiency and effectiveness of regulatory supervision across the PRA. Our vision is to be the PRA’s trusted partners in delivering innovative technology and data products that empower PRA colleagues with advanced tools for enhanced decision-making, effective oversight and driving operational efficiencies. RDI is made up of 3 hubs: Strategy and Innovation Hub AI and Analytics Hub Delivery and Governance Hub This role is part of the Delivery and Governance Hub on a 9-12-month maternity cover secondment. Job Description: Lead the delivery of strategic data and technology transformation initiatives within the PRA, with particular responsibility for the delivery of the Supervisory Analytics & Metrics (SAM) programme. The role is accountable for translating strategic objectives into deliverable outcomes, overseeing programme governance, managing complex stakeholder relationships, and ensuring the successful delivery of innovative data and analytics capabilities that improve supervisory effectiveness and efficiency.
