Manage programme risks, issues, dependencies and resource requirements, ensuring appropriate mitigations are in place and communicated to senior stakeholders. Drive delivery through Agile methodologies, promoting transparency, continuous improvement and effective prioritisation of work. Stakeholder Management and Influence Build and maintain strong relationships with senior stakeholders across the PRA, Technology, DAT and other Bank functions. Influence decision-making through effective communication, evidence-based recommendations and collaborative problem solving. Facilitate governance forums and boards, ensuring strategic decisions are informed, documented and progressed effectively. Represent programme interests in Bank-wide discussions and governance processes Team Leadership and Capability Development Lead and develop high-performing delivery teams, creating an inclusive and collaborative environment. Coach and support colleagues to build capability in programme delivery, Agile practices and stakeholder management. Shape programme structures, resource planning and workforce requirements to ensure sustainable delivery capacity. Foster effective collaboration across multiple directorates and disciplines. Governance, Risk and Assurance Establish and maintain effective programme governance, ensuring delivery remains aligned to strategic objectives. Provide clear and concise reporting to senior leadership forums. Promote robust decision-making, transparency and accountability across all aspects of programme delivery. Role Requirements: Minimum Criteria: Demonstrable experience of programme or change delivery in a complex organisational environment. Ability to manage delivery plans, risks, issues, dependencies and competing priorities. Experience working with stakeholders across business and technology functions Strong programme leadership experience, including leading large-scale data, technology or transformation initiatives from strategy through to delivery. Strong understanding of Agile delivery methods, delivery governance and assurance approaches, applying a Product-led approach by working closely with a Product Manager. Proven ability to lead delivery teams, manage complex dependencies and maintain momentum across multiple workstreams. Ability to translate strategic objectives into clear plans, outcomes and measurable delivery milestones. Desirable Criteria: Experience delivering cloud-based data and analytics platforms. item.title: Head of Department (x2 roles), Wholesale and Unauthorised Business Investigations
item.description: About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator ; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. Background We are looking to appoint two additional Heads of Department to help lead our Wholesale and Unauthorised Business Investigations (WUBI) directorate, joining the leadership team which is made up of two other Heads of Departments (HoDs) and the Director. Our efforts help to fight financial crime, disrupt harm, protect the interests of consumers, and ensure that markets work well and operate with integrity. WUBI conducts forensic investigations into regulatory breaches and criminal offences by firms and individuals operating in the wholesale arena, as well as those carrying on regulated activities without authorisation, in breach of the general prohibition. Typical WUBI cases include insider dealing, market manipulation, individual misconduct, fraud and scams, and organised crime activity linked to the financial services sector. The portfolio includes regulatory and criminal operations, civil proceedings and the FCA’s Proceeds of Crime team sits within WUBI. By working across the FCA and with domestic and international regulators and law enforcement, WUBI helps ensure a coordinated and effective response to threats facing UK markets and consumers, and disrupting criminal activity. The Role Reporting to the Director of WUBI, the Heads of Department ( HoDs) will be responsible for the development and delivery of the Enforcement strategy, in particular through ensuring investigations are delivered to a high standard. They will also play a key role in driving forward the FCA’s strategic work to fight financial crime and disrupt harm. The appointed candidates will be part of the Division’s senior leadership team and will take an active role supporting and challenging others to deliver the full range of the Division’s responsibilities (which also include Market Oversight and Intelligence). The candidates will be innovative, forward-thinking leaders who look across organisational boundaries, join up our work and drive forward the outcomes that matter most. Key responsibilities: Working with other Enforcement HoDs as part of a team to support the Director of WUBI in the delivery of the FCA’s work. Setting the strategic direction of the department (and with other senior management contributing to the strategic direction of the Division). Leading and inspiring a diverse, multi-disciplinary team of investigators. Promoting a culture of high performance, relying on coaching, influencing, and negotiating skills with a range of internal and external stakeholders Active management of a complex portfolio of investigations across WUBI to tight timeframes and which result in criminal, regulatory and civil action. Demonstrating clear operational grip and ensuring cases are delivered fairly, effectively and efficiently Collaborating across organisational boundaries to disrupt harm as early as possible, especially in relation to financial crime. Being accountable for divisional budget and resource management decisions as part of the senior divisional leadership team. What will the candidates get from the role? The successful candidates will: join the FCA’s senior leadership team at an exciting period of change for financial services and its regulation. lead a department of talented and experienced people, working collaboratively on significant projects and programmes get exposure to a broad range of issues and will contribute to the leadership team of both Enforcement and Market Oversight and the FCA, helping to shape and influence the organisation’s strategy. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Sound technical understanding of the regulatory framework in the UK and the FCA's place within it, with knowledge of the FCA’s powers and policies in relation to investigation and enforcement activity including criminal investigations and prosecutions. Significant people management and leadership experience, with a demonstrated ability to guide, motivate, and inspire large teams, while addressing performance concerns to build high performing teams. Extensive experience leading and overseeing complex investigations, with demonstrated clear operational grip Senior stakeholder management skills, with experience influencing internally & externally, and working across organisational boundaries to deliver cross-organisation projects. Ability to develop and implement change and process efficiency/improvements, delivering value for money and innovation Essential A clear track record of leading teams to deliver results against business priorities. A developed understanding of the regulatory and political environment in which the FCA operates, and an ability to build in-depth knowledge in this area. Ability to manage demanding situations, robustness in the face of challenge and able to make practical and balanced decisions quickly. Proficiency in maintaining strong working relationships across different business areas and to set joint goals for delivery. Negotiation and influencing skills – to deploy internally and externally. Ability to work as part of a senior leadership team with a wide range of responsibilities, supporting colleagues and the Director in the delivery of their work. Understanding how intelligence supports efforts to prevent and respond to criminal activity. Budget management and experience of managing external resources. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. If you have an accessibility requirement, disability, or condition that means you might require changes to the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter to discuss this further. Our aim is to make your application as easy as possible, and your recruiter will be happy to work with you to make any necessary arrangements where possible. Benefits Our competitive benefits scheme gives you the opportunity to create a personalised benefits package, tailored to suit your lifecycle. You can use this allowance to purchase additional benefits such as dental or cycle to work, or you have the option to top up your base salary by taking this as cash. Core benefits that you will receive as standard are: 30 days holiday per year plus bank holidays Private healthcare with Bupa A non-contributory Pension of at least 8% of basic salary each month (there are several contribution levels that increase depending on your age - up to 12% a month once you reach age 35) Life assurance of eight times your basic salary Income protection Conflicts of interest All applicants to the FCA are required to demonstrate that they do not have other interests likely to conflict with their responsibilities as an employee of the FCA. You should declare any potential conflict of interest as early as possible in the selection process, and also disclose information or personal connections that, if appointed, might be open to misperception. Any potential conflicts of interest will not prevent candidates going forward to interview but may, i

item.title: Senior Credit Rating Agency Supervision Associate
item.description: Job Title: Senior Credit Rating Agency Supervision Associate Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Infrastructure and Exchanges Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,200 and London £59,200 to £73,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Iona Magee via iona.magee@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. We are currently seeking a skilled individual to join the Benchmarks and Credit Rating Agencies Supervision team within the Capital Markets Department. The Capital Markets Department sits within SPC division at the FCA and is responsible for both benchmark and credit rating agencies supervision and policy. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Benchmarks and Credit Ratings Supervision Team is responsible for supervising UK-regulated benchmark administrators and CRAs in line with the applicable regulatory requirements and the FCA’s Approach to Supervision. Benchmark administrators produce benchmarks that are used across financial markets. Where they perform this role effectively, market participants can rely on accurate and representative measures of underlying market activity. CRAs play a key role in providing an assessment of the creditworthiness of governments, corporates and other issuers of securities. Where they perform this role effectively, investors are well-informed on the risks of investing in these assets and hence, capital is more efficiently allocated. These outcomes contribute particularly to the FCA’s statutory objective for market integrity and its consumer protection objective. Role responsibilities Lead the FCA’s supervisory relationships with assigned CRAs, using engagement and direct dialogue to support positive behavioural change and deliver effective regulatory outcomes Shape and deliver strategic supervisory initiatives across ratings processes, operational resilience and governance, helping to reduce harm and improve market integrity Apply expert judgement to identify emerging risks within credit ratings markets and support proportionate interventions that protect consumers and enhance confidence in the financial system Build close partnerships with senior stakeholders across the FCA, bringing insights together to inform supervisory priorities and decision-making Share expertise and contribute to a collaborative learning culture, supporting colleagues across Capital Markets and enhancing the FCA’s supervisory effectiveness Work closely with colleagues across supervisory teams to identify risks, solve complex challenges and deliver outcomes that help safeguard markets and improve the financial wellbeing of millions of consumers across the UK Skills required Minimum: Prior experience working in a regulatory or financial services position, such as credit rating agency, commercial or investment bank, asset management, law firm or any other regulatory body Prior experience working in an analytical role using a varied range of information, both qualitative and quantitative and using that to form judgements that balance a range of factors Essential: Thorough understanding of the CRAs business model, credit ratings processes and the potential risks associated with CRA activities Ability to lead and deliver projects effectively within agreed timelines while managing multiple priorities Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present clear, concise and well-reasoned arguments Ability to make informed and timely decisions, acting on their own initiative to identify key issues, navigate complexity and escalate matters where appropriate Well-developed organizational skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities and manage changing demands effectively Flexible and responsive approach, with the ability to respond positively to change and adjust working styles to meet evolving business needs Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively as part of a team, consistently supporting colleagues and contributing to the successful delivery of shared objectives Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser
item.description: Location: Westminster Contract : Fixed term for 6-12 months Salary: £47,609 per annum (Including London Weighting) About us The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. We work on behalf of our member councils to support, promote and improve local government. We are a politically led, cross-party organisation that works on behalf of councils to ensure local government has a strong, credible voice with national government. We influence and set the political agenda on the issues that matter to councils to help them deliver local solutions to national problems. We also provide councils with the tools and resources to respond to challenges present and emerging, and support improvement across the sector. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community to this high-profile role. About the role Reporting to the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, duties of the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser include: *Work collaboratively as part of the Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement team to contribute to the development and delivery of the LGA’s public affairs and campaigns activity. This will involve working with colleagues across the LGA to enhance the political influence and public profile of both the LGA and local government. *Contribute to the delivery of the LGA’s Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement approach by helping to influence parliamentary debates, select committees and legislation in order to secure positive change on behalf of local government. * Support delivery of the LGA’s Communications Strategy by building and maintaining key relationships in Parliament and with other relevant corporate stakeholders. *Support LGA councillors and member councils to engage with Parliament, including briefing senior LGA members and officials ahead of parliamentary inquiries and as part of the LGA’s party conference engagement. This will also involve working closely with the LGA’s Chair and members of the Senior Leadership Team. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement to organise high-impact public affairs events and ensure the LGA has a strong corporate profile at the autumn party conferences. This includes organising high-impact briefings to build the LGA’s network of support in Parliament, supporting the LGA’s annual local government parliamentary reception and organising Smith Square Debates. *Provide perceptive and insightful political intelligence and advice to identify opportunities for the LGA, strengthen the organisation’s public affairs profile and support wider communications activity. *Work with the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement and colleagues across the Communications Directorate to provide public affairs advice and support to member councils, including through the LGA’s Public Affairs Network. * Support the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement in ensuring that the Public Affairs team is the first point of contact for queries from MPs, peers, political parties, parliamentary staff, think tanks and stakeholders on LGA policy recommendations and local government issues. Promote and enhance the reputation of local government and, where necessary, help defend councils’ reputation. *Work with colleagues, as required by the Head of Public Affairs and Stakeholder Engagement, to produce regular forward-looking grids summarising, scheduling and coordinating future LGA public affairs and campaigning activity, announcements and other initiatives. *Undertake out-of-hours duties as necessary, including attending parliamentary, political, think tank and campaign-related events. The position is required to support immediate delivery needs The organisation is consulting on its operating model The grade and responsibilities are subject to confirmation Priority consideration may be given to employees at risk where they have the required qualifications and experience About you Based in the LGA’s office in Westminster, the Public Affairs and Campaigns Adviser will have: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, be highly motivated and able to work using your own initiative. An interest in developing your own networks within both political and communications circles. A strong commitment to personal and professional development achieved by maintaining regular communication with contacts in Parliament, Whitehall and stakeholders relevant to local government. Strong interpersonal skills and a proactive, team-oriented approach to working. A keen interest in networking and confidence to communicate with members of parliament, government ministers and officials, and leaders across local government. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. You must have the right to work in the UK, the LGA are unfortunately unable to offer sponsorship visas. Evidence for the right to work in the UK will be requested at the interview stage. Please note that, due to the nature of the role, applications from current serving councillors cannot be considered. To apply If you would like to be considered for the role, please complete the online form and include a supporting statement detailing how you meet the criteria for the role before the closing date. We are specifically assessing candidates against the following criteria: 1. Considerable experience working for a parliamentarian, select committee, government department or delivering public affairs in a lobbying/campaigning organisation or within local and regional government. 2. An excellent understanding of Westminster, Whitehall and local government, including the interface between local authorities, national government, political parties and opinion-formers. 3. Experience and evidence of success in positively influencing relevant opinion-formers, including influencing primary legislation, a parliamentary debate, a select committee report or working with parliamentarians to secure the tabling of parliamentary questions. 4. Evidence of success in working to deliver public affairs plans and corporate campaigns. 5. Experience in aligning public affairs and campaigning activity with colleagues in other disciplines, including media, policy and campaigns. 6. Ability to prioritise competing demands, within a pressured environment, and adopt a flexible approach to work and - when necessary - working hours. Closing Date: 01 October 2026, 5pm Interview Date: TBC We use anonymous recruitment, which is the practice of hiding candidates’ identities. This process involves removing any identifying information from candidates’ applications which includes names. At the LGA we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Our recruitment decisions are based on fair, open competition, with appointment on merit. ***The LGA are proud to be awarded a “Disability Confident Leader”. Please contact us via *** Recruitment@local.gov.ukif you require a reasonable adjustment, which is a change to the format or conditions of the recruitment process to accommodate any disability-related needs you may have. Our benefits LGA annual leave entitlement is 29 days, rising to 31 days after three years’ service and to 33 days after five years’ service, plus all UK public holidays (pro rata for fixed term and part time contracts).* Flexible & agile working – office-based staff are required to work in the LGA’s London office two days per week as a minimum, subject to business need and this may vary significantly between different roles and from week to week. Future development – face-to-face and virtual courses are scheduled in line with developmental goals The LGA offers 24/7 access to a free, confidential employee assistance programme managed by Health Assured. This service is also available for Dependants. Family friendly policies For more of LGA’s benefits and working with us, please view our webpage https://www.local.gov.uk/benefits-and-working-lga Our values & behaviours Our Values and Behaviours are there to give us an understanding of who we are as an organisation and who we want to be. They are a framework to help us understand: how we work with each other how we work with our members and stakeholders our expectations for ourselves and each other Our values are: Collaboration – We value collaboration, to pursue shared goals by encouraging and utilising diverse perspectives and working with internal and external colleagues across the organisation. Inclusion – We value inclusion, where everyone feels valued, understood, and supported to contribute meaningfully. Ambition – We value ambition, reflecting our desire to achieve best possible outcomes for local government, communities, and individuals. Respect – We value respect, to ensure fairness, recognition, and shared accountability.

item.title: Head of Department: AI & Technology Security Operations
item.description: The FCA has retained Global Resourcing to manage this role; send applications directly to Global Resourcing . About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and AI and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a permanent Head of AI & Technology Security Operations. This role is designed for an experienced manager, senior technical specialist, or existing Head of Department with proven experience of leading teams and operating at scale in a rapidly evolving digital and AI-driven operating environment. The successful candidate will strengthen their strategic and operational leadership while overseeing high-tempo, service-critical digital and AI operations. The Head of AI & Technology Security Operations is accountable for ensuring that the FCA’s technology estate — including rapidly expanding AI capabilities — is robust, secure, and able to withstand, detect, and recover from disruption, failure, or exploitation. The role brings together operational resilience, infrastructure governance, supplier oversight, and enterprise technology and AI-specific vulnerability management, ensuring that both traditional infrastructure and AI-enabled systems are designed, operated, and governed to remain safe, dependable, and trustworthy under stress. Working in close collaboration with C&IR (Cyber and Information Resilience), this HoD plays a critical leadership role in implementing and managing the technology controls needed to anticipate and mitigate AI-driven risks, including model vulnerabilities, upstream dependency risks, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, and control failures arising from increased autonomy and scale. This role will be responsible for leading, motivating and directing the department (~70FTE) across London, Leeds, & Edinburgh; and managing the FCA’s critical Digital and AI systems, including AI live service, Service Desk, Incident Management, Cyber Security Operations and Supplier Management. This is a fantastic development opportunity which will help to build expertise, experience and career skills in a senior, challenging and highly visible role. The role will be reporting to the Chief Information Officer, and sit in the wider Data, Technology, and Innovation Division. What will the candidate get from the role? As Head of AI & Technology Security Operations, you will join the DTI senior leadership team at a pivotal moment in the FCA’s evolution, supporting its ambition to become a forward-thinking, AI-enabled and data-driven regulator. You will lead a skilled multidisciplinary department, working across high-impact digital and AI initiatives to strengthen technology and AI risk management, improve resilience and enable the safe adoption of emerging technologies. Collaborating closely with Cyber & Information Resilience, DTI leadership, product teams and front-line divisions, you will play a key role in driving meaningful change and reinforcing the FCA’s reputation as a trusted, innovative regulator. Key responsibilities will include: Leading the development and operation of the FCA’s AI vulnerability and threat management capability, identifying and mitigating risks linked to AI model weaknesses, adversarial threats, automation and agentic AI systems. Establishing clear frameworks and controls for the safe deployment of AI, including human oversight, monitoring, explainability, version control, containment and safe shutdown mechanisms. Maintaining effective AI governance, including ownership, inventory management, risk classification and oversight of AI-enabled services across the organisation. Acting as accountable owner for technology and AI risk, including control design, testing, assurance activity and risk acceptance decisions. Providing clear, metrics-led reporting to senior committees and Board-level forums on risk posture, emerging threats, control effectiveness and material gaps. Overseeing critical third-party and AI supply chain dependencies, including cloud platforms, AI model providers, managed services and data sources. Ensuring supplier, concentration and substitution risks are understood, monitored and managed effectively. Owning technology continuity strategies across data, digital and AI services, ensuring critical services can withstand disruption, degrade safely and recover effectively. Overseeing scenario testing, failover design, recovery validation and core service operations, including incident, problem and change management. Leading and developing multidisciplinary teams across technology risk, AI operations, supplier management, continuity and live service operations. Building strong capability, clear accountability and a culture where secure, resilient and dependable systems are a shared responsibility. Representing the FCA externally with government, regulators, industry bodies and standards organisations on technology, AI and operational resilience. Managing team budget, headcount, resources and IT supplier spend of approximately £80m. Championing innovation, continuous improvement and the safe adoption of emerging technologies to strengthen resilience, efficiency and value for money. This is a high-profile leadership role with enterprise-scale accountability, operating at the intersection of AI, cyber, technology, supplier and operational risk, with a direct contribution to the FCA’s regulatory credibility and public trust. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Hands on experience, however recent, with AI or agentic AI technologies. Familiarity with UK regulatory frameworks relating to operational resilience, critical third parties, cyber resilience, and AI governance. Experience within financial services, government, regulatory, or other highly regulated environments Essential Strong stakeholder management, capable of engaging with and developing strong trusting relationships with stakeholders from across a business organisation and at senior levels, as well as third parties. Evidence of managing supplier relationships across a complex supplier and contract environment Knowledge of NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, ISO 27001, DORA, or similar frameworks. An ability to manage and control risk, embed good practice, and drive change where necessary. In-depth working knowledge of multiple domains, including Engineering, DevOps, AI, Cyber Security and Cloud technology platforms. Experience of driving change and process efficiency/improvements, delivering value for money and innovation. Ability to inclusively lead a large group of talented individuals with a wide variety of professional expertise, experience, and backgrounds. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. As part of the FCA’s on-going commitment to develop our national presence, most of our vacancies are now open to working in our Edinburgh, Leeds or London offices. This means that as part of the application process you will be able to select your preference of which office location you would like to work from. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. item.title: Programme Manager – SEND
item.description: Location: Home based Contract : 8 month secondment or FTC Salary: £78,551 to £89,005 About us The Local Government Association (LGA) is the national membership body for local authorities. We work on behalf of our member councils to support, promote and improve local government. We are a politically led, cross-party organisation that works on behalf of councils to ensure local government has a strong, credible voice with national government. We influence and set the political agenda on the issues that matter to councils to help them deliver local solutions to national problems. We also provide councils with the tools and resources to respond to challenges present and emerging, and support improvement across the sector. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community to this high-profile role. About the role The LGA is seeking to appoint a programme manager with experience of working in SEND system, within local government at a senior, strategic level. Working closely with senior colleagues within the LGA with responsibility for the children’s services improvement programme you will act as a key interface between the LGA and local authorities and their partners. You will lead the delivery and implementation of a Department for Education grant focussed on leadership development in SEND. You will work with key sector partners, including local authorities, DfE, ADCS, health, education settings and parents/carers, to design and deliver improvement activity that strengthens leadership capacity in local SEND systems. Your success will be determined by your ability to understand and respond to the highly challenging, politically sensitive and high-profile SEND environment in order to manage complexities and risk, and successfully maintain a positive reputation for the LGA with its member authorities. About you * You will have a comprehensive understanding about how local areas, through multi agency arrangements, provide services for children with SEND and the complexities, challenges and opportunities this presents. * You will have a comprehensive understanding of local government and the wider public sector and how the delivery of services for children sits within this. * You will be confident and credible in working with leading members, chief executives, directors of children’s services and other partner system leaders * You will hit the ground running, using your abilities and experience to effectively manage and maintain relationships with local authorities and the Department for Education to ensure effective delivery of the children’s improvement programme. You must have the right to work in the UK, the LGA are unfortunately unable to offer sponsorship visas. Evidence for the right to work in the UK will be requested at the interview stage. To apply If you would like to be considered for the role, please complete the online form and include a supporting statement detailing how you meet the criteria for the role before the closing date. We are specifically assessing candidates against the following criteria: * Proven knowledge and expertise in relation to the national policy context affecting SEND services * Record of achievement in complex political environments, in local government SEND services * Understanding of the key issues, priorities and pressures affecting local government including the policy and improvement agenda * Political sensitivity, and the ability to exercise appropriate discretion and judgement on issues of significance and importance, and when dealing with politicians and officials * Practical experience of designing interventions and innovative solutions to complex issues affecting SEND * Confident and resilient with excellent people skills, able to develop positive internal and external relationships; Strong team player able to build alliances and lead from within To help us anonymise applications efficiently, please ensure your CV meets the following formatting requirements: * Please use standard fonts such as Arial, Times New Roman, or Calibri * Avoid complex graphics, logos, or images where possible * Keep formatting simple – use basic bullet points and standard paragraph formatting * Save your CV as a standard PDF file * Ensure the file size is under 5MB * Avoid unusual page layouts or multi-column designs * Use standard text colours (e.g., black, or dark grey) CVs that do not meet these guidelines may not be processed correctly by our system. Closing Date: 5pm, 24 September Interview Date: week commencing 28 September, interviews will be virtual Interview Panel: TBC We use anonymous recruitment, which is the practice of hiding candidates’ identities. This process involves removing any identifying information from candidates’ applications which includes names. At the LGA we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Our recruitment decisions are based on fair, open competition, with appointment on merit. The LGA are proud to be awarded a “Disability Confident Leader”. Please contact us via Recruitment@local.gov.uk if you require a reasonable adjustment, which is a change to the format or conditions of the recruitment process to accommodate any disability-related needs you may have. Our benefits LGA annual leave entitlement is 29 days, rising to 31 days after three years’ service and to 33 days after five years’ service, plus all UK public holidays (pro rata for fixed term and part time contracts).* Flexible & agile working – office-based staff are required to work in the LGA’s London office two days per week as a minimum, subject to business need and this may vary significantly between different roles and from week to week. Future development – face-to-face and virtual courses are scheduled in line with developmental goals The LGA offers 24/7 access to a free, confidential employee assistance programme managed by Health Assured. Family friendly policies For more of LGA’s benefits and working with us, please view our webpage https://www.local.gov.uk/benefits-and-working-lga Our values & behaviours Our Values and Behaviours are there to give us an understanding of who we are as an organisation and who we want to be. They are a framework to help us understand: how we work with each other how we work with our members and stakeholders our expectations for ourselves and each other Our values are: Collaboration – We value collaboration, to pursue shared goals by encouraging and utilising diverse perspectives and working with internal and external colleagues across the organisation. Inclusion – We value inclusion, where everyone feels valued, understood, and supported to contribute meaningfully. Ambition – We value ambition, reflecting our desire to achieve best possible outcomes for local government, communities, and individuals. Respect – We value respect, to ensure fairness, recognition, and shared accountability.
